Exercise A

What Does It Mean to Be Scottish?

Read the text carefully, then answer the comprehension questions using the dropdown menus.

Reading Text

What does it mean to be Scottish? For many people, Scottish identity is about much more than living inside a border on a map. It is a mixture of history, landscape, language and a strong sense of belonging.

Language plays an important part in this identity. As well as English and Scottish Gaelic, many Scots speak Scots, a language closely related to English but with its own distinctive words. For example, a child might be called a "bairn", a small amount is a "wee bit", and to be tired is to be "wabbit". Although some people once saw Scots as simply "bad English", it is now recognised and celebrated as a language in its own right.

Scotland's relationship with the rest of the United Kingdom is another key part of its identity. While Scotland has been part of the UK since 1707, it has kept its own legal system, its own education system and its own church. In 2014, Scots even voted in a referendum on whether to become an independent country. In the end, the majority chose to remain in the UK, but the debate showed how strongly many people feel about their nation.
